newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India rallies but no sustained run seen.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India rallies but no sustained run seen.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) rallied on the back of a stronger local market on Thursday but traders said few believed that snapping the market's longterm losing streak.
"It is a bounce as locals cover short positions and market makers bid up more in hope for tomorrow than anything else," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 1.82 points, or 3.47 percent, at 54.15 points, with the premium over the local market at 13.96 percent compared with Wednesday's 13.39 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 67.16 percent, 2.45 percent, to 2,812.22.
"No one is going to be a buyer of this market. People are just holding their books flat and waiting for the Christmas break," said a trader.
The Capel Indian GDR index has fallen 24.3 percent from the 71.53 point level of January 2, the first trading day of this year.
Traders were not surprised that BPL Cellular had called off its $200 million issue of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

"The lead had tried to ram it down investors' throats. But in these market conditions it is difficult to see a good quality issue getting away, let alone one which was criticised by its auditors," said one.
KPMG highlighted the company's low level of working capital and large capital needs.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 0.63 points, 1.01 percent, at 61.51, a premium of 29.45 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 9.57 points to a provisional 706.30.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 1.83 points, 1.89 percent, at 94.81, a premium of 4.32 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index lost 24.15 points to 6,919.49. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
